title: Sharpness of Probability-of-Causation Bounds for Multi-Valued Treatments and Outcomes via Flows
banked_reason: D0.5: sound sharp scalar conjunction interval, but paper_score_ceiling 7.0 is below the 7.4 field floor and no bounded same-scope repair can clear it.
gap_reasons: The contribution remains confined to one scalar conjunction under common-population consistency-only margins and does not establish simultaneous sharpness for multiple response patterns or policy utilities.
The support result determines only the order between mr and 2mr-m, while the confidence procedure is conservative and has no efficiency or width guarantee.
These limitations and the absence of a developed application keep the package below flagship significance despite clearing the field-level floor.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved the complete sharp scalar interval, constructive endpoint laws, exact evaluation and certificates, and a certificate-preserving O(mr) support bound; the citation and mathematics panels passed. The field claim collapsed on scope rather than correctness: reaching the floor would require a new simultaneous multi-query or policy-utility result, stronger inference, and a developed application.
tldr: Common-population observational and single-treatment intervention margins determine the exact identified interval for every finite-alphabet scalar conjunction probability of causation.  The Shu--Wang--Li endpoints are attained for every compatible real input by indicator coarsening, upper intersection packing, and a deleted-diagonal lower flow with a residual-failure invariant.  For rational inputs, sorting evaluates the endpoints and explicit laws of support at most \(N_\star\) preserve the relevant input denominator grid.  A separate exact margin-kernel step preserves the active-affine or minimum-cut certificate while constructively compressing either endpoint law to at most \(2mr-m\) atoms of polynomial encoding length; no denominator-divisibility claim is made after compression.  Thus \(mr\leq s_\star(m,r,k)\leq2mr-m\), and block-multinomial confidence-region inversion supplies uniform finite-sample coverage while Cheng--Mao--Pearl--Li retain credit for directional inference.
gap: Shu--Wang--Li prove all-dimensional validity but leave pointwise tightness open, while Xie--Li's constructive proof is binary and generic response-signature programs conceal the scalar geometry in exponentially many response states.
fill: The paper derives the exact indicator lifting, the packing and flow endpoint laws, the min-cut and sorted duals, audited polynomial witness complexity, and a boundary-safe finite-sample inversion of the resulting sharp interval.
